traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 110 Begoniaceae: undershrubs or herbs, mostly succulent, the stems jointed; leaves alternate, simple, often lopsided; stipules free, falling; flowers on one plant in two sexes, regular or irregular, mostly in cymes in the leaf axils, showy; the male with 2 (rarely 5) sepals and 0 to 5 petals and many stamens. The inferior ovary and the winged capsule are from common knowledge (the account is cut short in the copy read), inferred, not traced.
